meta.title: Catalyst Builder – Dependency injection for Dart
meta.description: A lightweight, easy-to-use dependency injection container builder for Dart. Annotate your services with @Service and let build_runner generate the container for you.

docs.indexIntro: Guides that take you from an empty project to a booted service container, plus the notes for moving between major versions.

hero.lede: A lightweight, easy-to-use dependency injection container builder for Dart. Annotate your services with `@Service` and let build_runner generate the container for you.

how.title: Three steps from annotation to a fully wired app.

steps.title: Mark your services
steps.body: Decorate classes with `@Service` and your entry point with `@GenerateServiceContainerPlugin`.

steps.title: Run build_runner
steps.body: The builder writes a `*.catalyst_builder.plugin.g.dart` file next to your annotated entry point.

steps.title: Boot the container
steps.body: Create a `ServiceContainer`, register the generated plugin, boot it – then resolve anything.

features.title: Everything you need. Nothing you have to wire by hand.
features.aside: Built around SOLID principles and dependency inversion – so your app stays testable as it grows.

items.title: Compile-time generation
items.body: The container is generated with build_runner – no runtime reflection, a perfect fit for Flutter.

items.title: Annotation-driven
items.body: Declare services with `@Service`, or map them centrally with `@ServiceMap`.

items.title: Program to interfaces
items.body: Expose an implementation under its abstraction with `exposeAs` and swap it anytime.

items.title: Plugin architecture
items.body: Each package can ship its own generated container plugin – compose them in your root app.

items.title: Runs everywhere
items.body: Pure Dart and Flutter: Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS and Linux.

items.title: Lightweight & open
items.body: Small footprint, full pub points, MIT licensed – use it in any project, commercial or not.

packages.title: Generate where you need it. Depend on contracts everywhere else.

items.body: Use it in your root package or a plugin package to generate the `ServiceContainerPlugin`.
Use it in packages that don't generate a container themselves but provide services that can be resolved.

quickstart.title: Up and running in under a minute.
quickstart.lede: Add the packages, annotate your entry point, generate – done. The docs walk through a complete Flutter app.

cta.title: Let the builder do the wiring.
cta.lede: Free and open source. Star the repo, open an issue or send a pull request – contributions are welcome.
